jobs.description: Become a part of our caring community Become a part of our caring community and help us put health first.We are seeking a skilled Decision Intelligence Engineer to design, train, and continuously improve the reinforcement learning policy at the heart of Humana's Next Best Action platform. In this role you will own the full RL development lifecycle from feature engineering and reward design through distributed training, evaluation, and production deployment ensuring that every decision the platform makes for our 8 million members is informed by a policy that learns and improves with every interaction. You will work at the intersection of healthcare outcomes and decision engineering, translating member journey data into durable, explainable, and auditable decisioning intelligence. This role is hands-on and research-oriented: you will implement and evaluate RL algorithms, instrument training pipelines, collaborate closely with data and platform engineers, and ensure the model operates correctly within the constraints of clinical eligibility rules and program-specific reward structures. Key Responsibilities Reinforcement Learning Model Development Design, implement, and evaluate RL algorithms suited to long-horizon, sparse-reward healthcare decisioning, including policy gradient methods (PPO, A3C), value-based approaches (DQN, Q-learning), and offline RL methods (CQL, Decision Transformer). Define and maintain the member state representation and action space, evolving both as new programs and data sources are onboarded. Apply the Bellman equation, reward shaping, and constraint mapping to encode clinical eligibility, suppression rules, and program-specific objectives directly into the learning objective. Manage exploration-exploitation tradeoffs appropriate for a production healthcare environment where poorly explored actions have real member impact. Model Evaluation and Production Safety Build simulation and backtesting environments to evaluate policy quality before production promotion, using historical member journey data. Diagnose and remediate common RL failure modes: policy collapse, credit assignment errors across long member journeys, and distributional shift between training and serving populations. Define reward threshold criteria and automated evaluation gates within the nightly Databricks training workflow; block promotion of underperforming policies to MLflow production. Instrument training runs with MLflow tracking hyperparameters, reward curves, action distribution, and feature importance for every training cycle. Training Pipeline Engineering Own the nightly Databricks training workflow: feature engineering from Gold Activity History and Gold Patient Profile, state vector normalization, distributed RL training via Ray RLlib, and batch scoring of all 8M eligible members. Collaborate with the Data Engineering team (Decisioning Team 2) to ensure training inputs are correctly joined, reward signals are accurately computed from disposition outcomes, and the feature pipeline is reproducible and auditable. Write production-quality PySpark feature engineering jobs; maintain data lineage through Databricks Unity Catalog. Manage model artifacts, versioning, and lifecycle in the MLflow Model Registry; ensure rollback capability is maintained at all times. Multi-Agent and Constraint-Aware Decisioning Apply multi-agent RL concepts (MARL via PettingZoo) where member household or population-level coordination is required. Implement constraint mapping to enforce hard business rules — member caps, cooldown periods, clinical eligibility — as constraints within the RL objective rather than downstream filters. Collaborate with the Rules Engine team to ensure Drools eligibility guards and RL policy priorities are correctly aligned and do not conflict. Collaboration and Governance Partner with Decisioning Team 1 (Decision Engine, Rules Engine) to ensure model outputs integrate cleanly with the real-time decisioning hot path and that scored recommendations cached in Redis are correctly structured and interpreted. Collaborate with platform architects to define feedback loop contracts: how disposition outcomes flow from Kafka back through Databricks Delta Live Tables into the next training cycle. Document model behavior, known limitations, and failure modes for clinical and compliance stakeholders; support explainability requirements for member-facing decisions. Utilize AI-assisted engineering tools for scaffolding, testing, and documentation; ensure all core model logic and reward design remain human-authored and subject to rigorous peer review. Use your skills to make an impact Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in computer science or related field 8+ years of software engineering experience building and operating large-scale production systems, with emphasis on data-intensive platforms, recommendation systems, or optimization engines serving millions of users. 3+ years of hands-on experience implementing reinforcement learning or deep learning systems in production policy gradient methods (PPO, A3C), value-based approaches (DQN, Q-learning), or offline RL algorithms (CQL, Decision Transformer). Deep familiarity with the Bellman equation, reward shaping, exploration-exploitation tradeoff, and constraint mapping in real-world RL systems. Demonstrated ability to diagnose RL-specific failure modes: policy collapse, credit assignment issues, and distributional shift across large populations. Proficiency in Python 3.x; experience with PyTorch or TensorFlow for policy network implementation. Experience with Ray RLlib for distributed RL training at scale. Experience with Databricks, PySpark, and Delta Lake for large-scale ML pipelines processing tens of millions of records. Experience with MLflow for experiment tracking, model registry, and artifact management. Track record of shipping ML systems that operate reliably under production load — not just research or prototype work. Preferred Qualifications Experience with multi-agent RL frameworks (PettingZoo or equivalent). Familiarity with probabilistic modeling, Markov Decision Processes, and linear programming for constraint-aware action selection. Experience operating RL systems in regulated domains — healthcare, finance, or insurance — where member safety, auditability, and explainability are requirements. Experience with Gymnasium for simulation environment development and backtesting. Familiarity with Kafka-based feedback loops and how disposition signals feed RL retraining pipelines. OpenTelemetry instrumentation experience for ML training pipeline observability. Additional Information This role is not eligible for work visa sponsorship. jobs.description: Amazon Customer Service supports customers around the world through one of the world’s largest and most diverse customer service workforces. As AI fundamentally changes how customer service work is performed, it also creates an opportunity to reinvent how associates learn, develop their capabilities, receive coaching, and continuously improve. The Associate Development team is building the next generation of learning, coaching and performance experiences for Amazon Customer Service Associates. We are looking for a Software Development Engineer to help build these systems from the ground up. This is a highly greenfield opportunity. Rather than digitizing traditional training and coaching processes, we are rethinking how associate development should work in an AI-native world. What does an associate need to learn before doing a job? What can they learn through experience? What should AI provide in the flow of work? How can we understand an associate’s evolving capabilities and use that understanding to personalize development? How can generative AI help provide timely, relevant and effective coaching at the scale of a global workforce? Imagine systems that continuously learn from an associate’s experience and outcomes, identify where they would benefit from development, and deliver personalized learning or AI-powered coaching. The outcomes of those interventions can then become new evidence about the associate, creating a closed loop that gets smarter over time. As an SDE on this team, you will help define and build the technical foundations that make this possible. You will work on problems spanning generative AI, personalization, intelligent recommendations, learning and coaching systems, experimentation, data and distributed systems. You will have the opportunity to influence architecture at an early stage rather than inherit a predetermined technical solution. You will partner closely with Product, Science, UX and engineering teams across Amazon to turn ambiguous customer problems into scalable technical solutions. The systems you build have the potential to shape how Customer Service Associates around the world develop and succeed at work. This is an opportunity for an engineer who enjoys zero-to-one problems, emerging AI technologies, large-scale systems and building products with direct human impact. Key job responsibilities - Design and build scalable services and experiences that power personalized learning, coaching and associate development across Amazon Customer Service. - Build AI-powered coaching capabilities, including applications of generative AI that can understand context, generate relevant guidance and adapt experiences to individual associate needs. - Develop systems that connect signals about associate capability and performance with the right development intervention at the right time. - Help create closed-loop systems that measure the outcomes of learning and coaching interventions and use that evidence to continuously improve future recommendations. - Work with Product and Science partners to translate emerging models and experimentation into reliable production systems. - Make foundational architectural decisions for a greenfield product space while determining where existing Amazon capabilities can be reused or evolved. - Design APIs, data models and integration patterns that allow Associate Development capabilities to interact with associate context, workflow and other Customer Service systems. - Build mechanisms for experimentation, measurement and observability so we can understand whether the experiences we create actually improve associate and customer outcomes. - Deliver secure, reliable and globally scalable systems while maintaining a high bar for operational excellence. A day in the life You might start the day working with a scientist on how an AI coaching experience can use an associate’s recent performance context to generate more useful coaching. Later, you could whiteboard an architecture for measuring whether that coaching actually changed future performance, review an API contract with another CS platform team, and prototype a new generative-AI capability. Because the space is early, you won’t simply be executing against a fully specified roadmap. You will help answer fundamental technical questions, prototype alternatives, make architecture decisions, and turn successful experiments into production systems capable of serving associates globally. About the team The Associate Experience (AE) team is building the future of work for Amazon Customer Service Associates. Our vision is to create a trusted Customer Service experience by enabling associates to succeed as the role evolves toward complex and non-deterministic problem solving. Within AE, the Associate Development team is reinventing how associates learn, develop and improve, moving beyond one-size-fits-all training and coaching towards, personalized development powered by AI. Engineers joining the team will shape foundational architecture, drive technology choices, and build AI-powered products from the ground up for one of the world's largest customer service workforces.

This role is open to candidates based in Europe; Warsaw is preferred, where several of the people you'll work with are based.

Review fraud signals regularly, adding, removing and refining them to distinguish suspicious activity from legitimate users. Signals under consideration include IP spoofing, VPN use and unusual play patterns.

Identify gaps in the available signals and recommend third-party tools for the product roadmap where they would help.

Hands-on experience using data to investigate fraud and shape detection or prevention decisions, not just working alongside a fraud team.
Experience designing or improving fraud signals, user segments or review processes, with an interest in how those decisions change as tactics evolve.
The ability to work with product and other teams to turn analysis into operational fraud controls.

jobs.description: TL;DR: Brazil is one of Lovable's largest and fastest-growing markets, and it got there almost entirely on its own energy. The community runs its own Lovable Days. A Lovable Summit exists because Brazilian builders willed it into existence. The title says Growth Lead, but make no mistake: this is our general manager for Brazil. You'll own the market like a founder and carry the commercial judgment of someone who has opened Brazil for technology companies before. You know which doors to open, which to keep closed, and when the timing is right for each bet. You'll sit inside Product & Engineering because Brazil grows through Product-led Growth, and the product is one of your commercial levers: if checkout doesn't speak Pix or parcelamento, if BRL pricing is wrong, you drive the fix. WHY LOVABLE? Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started. We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams worldwide. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world. Brazil is one of our largest and fastest-growing markets, with millions of founders, students, freelancers, and small businesses building on their own, plus an enterprise and public sector hungry to build. Whoever takes this role will not inherit a playbook. They will write the one everyone else copies. WHAT YOU WILL OWN - The Brazil P&L mindset, end to end: Acquisition, activation, retention, and monetization. One market, full funnel, your number, your bets. - The commercial strategy: Decide where Lovable plays first: SMB, enterprise, education, public sector, partnerships. Sequence the bets, say no to the wrong ones, and open the doors that matter through your own network. - The Brazilian ecosystem: From boardrooms and executive networks to Campus Party, Web Summit Rio, South Summit, Gramado Summit, community-run Lovable events, and the WhatsApp groups where Brazil actually lives. - Product changes that unlock the market: Talk to users and buyers constantly, then drive what ships with product and engineering: Pix and parcelamento, BRL pricing and packaging, PT-BR onboarding, templates, and the integrations Brazilian companies expect. WHAT YOU ARE You've done this before. You've opened or scaled the Brazilian market for technology companies, and you carry the scar tissue and the network to prove it. - Commercially mature: A decade or more of building technology businesses in Brazil, ideally including executive roles (CIO, CTO, country or commercial leadership) and board exposure. You know the right people, and more importantly, you know which conversations to have and which to skip. - A strategic operator: You think in bets and sequencing. You can articulate what Lovable should optimize for in Brazil, and what it should deliberately ignore for now. - Technically savvy: You're credible with engineers, understand PLG mechanics, and use Lovable yourself. You don't need to write the code, but you understand exactly what the product needs to win here. - Native or near-native in Portuguese and fluent in English, our company language. - A builder at heart: Titles aside, you prefer doing over coordinating. There is no Brazil playbook at Lovable yet. That's the point. WHAT THIS ROLE IS NOT - Not "run Brazilian social media." - Not "translate our global marketing calendar." - Not "send HQ a deck about Brazil." You have the freedom, and the responsibility, to set the commercial strategy, shape the product, and define how Lovable shows up in Brazil. The goal is simple: make Brazil one of Lovable's strongest markets in the world. ABOUT YOUR APPLICATION - Don't send us a cover letter. Build something on Lovable and send us the link in the application form, plus a short note (Portuguese or English, your call) on the bets you believe Lovable should and should not make in Brazil over the next 18 months. - Please submit your application in English. It’s our company language, so you’ll be speaking lots of it if you join. - We treat all candidates equally - if you’re interested, please apply through our careers portal.
